title.zh: 卷320 列傳一百七 三宝 永贵 蔡新 程景伊 梁国治 英廉 彭元瑞 纪昀 陆锡熊 陆费墀
title.en: Volume 320 Biographies 107: San Bao, Yong Gui, Cai Xin, Cheng Jingyi, Liang Guozhi, Ying Lian, Peng Yuanrui, Ji Yun, Lu Xixiong, Lu Feichi
title.raw: 卷320 列傳一百七 三宝 永贵 蔡新 程景伊 梁国治 英廉 彭元瑞 纪昀 陆锡熊 陆费墀

sentences.zh: 三寶，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲正紅旗人。

translations.literal: San Bao, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: San Bao, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年繙譯進士，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Qianlong reign he passed the translator jinshi examination and was appointed a Grand Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 4 (1739) he earned jinshi through the translation examination and was appointed a drafter in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 襲世管佐領。

translations.literal: He inherited a hereditary company commander's post.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to a hereditary company commandership.

sentences.zh: 遷內閣侍讀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a reader in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to a reader in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為湖北驛鹽道。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Hubei Post and Salt Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as intendant of the Hubei Post and Salt Circuit.

sentences.zh: 入補戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He returned to fill a vacancy as a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital to fill a directorship in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 師徵準噶爾，命赴北路董達什達瓦游牧。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against the Dzungars, he was ordered to go to the northern route to supervise herds at Dongdashidawa.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dzungar campaign he was ordered to the northern front to oversee pastoral herds at Dongdashidawa.

sentences.zh: 擢直隸布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to Zhili provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，上幸熱河，坐蹕路不修，命以道銜駐哈密。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the emperor visited Rehe, for failure to maintain the imperial procession route he was ordered to remain at Hami with intendant's rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 26, while the emperor was at Rehe, San Bao was punished for neglecting repairs along the imperial route and was sent to Hami with intendant's rank.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，起四川布政使，更湖北、湖南、貴州諸省。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was recalled as Sichuan administration commissioner, then moved through Hubei, Hunan, and Guizhou provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 29 he was reappointed Sichuan administration commissioner and subsequently served in Hubei, Hunan, and Guizhou in turn.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，擢山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was promoted to governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 37 he was appointed governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，移浙江。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was moved to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 42 he was made governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 閱兵，衡州協副將海福、沅州協副將洪昌運皆衰老，三寶請以海福內授旗員，昌運令休致。

translations.literal: When reviewing troops, he found that Hengzhou garrison deputy commander Haifu and Yuanzhou garrison deputy commander Hong Changyun were both aged; San Bao requested that Haifu be given an internal banner appointment and that Changyun be ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: On troop inspection he found the Hengzhou and Yuanzhou garrison deputy commanders, Haifu and Hong Changyun, both too old for duty; he asked that Haifu be reassigned within the banners and that Changyun be retired.

sentences.zh: 上以偏護滿洲，顯分軒輊，拒不允。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that he was partial to Manchus and showed obvious favoritism, refused to approve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that he was favoring Manchus and showing clear partiality, and refused.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，授東閣大學士，兼禮部尚書，督湖廣如故。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was appointed Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary and concurrently Minister of Rites, continuing as governor-general of Huguang as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 44 he was made Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary and concurrent Minister of Rites while retaining the Huguang governor-generalship.

sentences.zh: 旋移閩浙總督。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to the Fujian-Zhejiang governor-generalship.

sentences.zh: 浙江海塘自老鹽倉以上皆柴塘，上南巡，諭改築石塘。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang seawalls above Laoyancang were all wattled embankments; on the southern tour the emperor ordered them rebuilt as stone dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Above Laoyancang the Zhejiang coast was protected by wattled seawalls; during his southern tour the emperor ordered them replaced with stone dikes.

sentences.zh: 三寶疏言：「時方大汛，未宜更動。

translations.literal: San Bao memorialized: "At present the great flood season is at hand; it is not suitable to make changes.
translations.idiomatic: San Bao memorialized: "The great flood season is upon us; this is no time for major works.

sentences.zh: 當於柴塘內下椿築石，而以柴塘為外護。」

translations.literal: Stone should be piled within the wattled dikes, using the wattled dikes as an outer shield."
translations.idiomatic: Stone piles should be driven inside the wattled embankments, leaving the wattled works as an outer barrier."

sentences.zh: 會上亦降旨令留柴塘為重關保障，與三寶議合。

translations.literal: The emperor also issued an edict ordering the wattled dikes kept as a major line of defense, which accorded with San Bao's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered that the wattled dikes be retained as a second line of defense, in agreement with San Bao's plan.

sentences.zh: 旋命入閣治事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered to enter the Grand Council and handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to the Grand Council to conduct state business.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王亶望以贓敗，三寶坐未舉劾，部議當奪職，上命留任。

translations.literal: When Governor Wang Tanwang was ruined by corruption, San Bao was held culpable for failing to impeach him; the ministry proposed dismissal, but the emperor ordered him retained.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Wang Tanwang fell in a corruption scandal, San Bao was faulted for not having impeached him; although the ministry recommended dismissal, the emperor kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 尋復令在上書房總師傅上行走。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again ordered to serve on duty under the chief tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned again to assist the chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，扈蹕熱河，以疾還京師。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he accompanied the emperor to Rehe, then returned to the capital on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 49 he escorted the emperor to Rehe, then returned to Beijing because of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡文敬。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Wénjìng.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Wénjìng (Cultivated and Reverent).

sentences.zh: 三寶喜讀宋諸儒書，大節不苟。

translations.literal: San Bao delighted in reading the Song Neo-Confucians and was unbending in major principles.
translations.idiomatic: San Bao loved the Song Neo-Confucian masters and would not compromise on matters of principle.

sentences.zh: 為直隸布政使時，高宗幸熱河，至密雲，值大霖雨，水盛漲。

translations.literal: When he was Zhili administration commissioner, the Gaozong Emperor visited Rehe; reaching Miyun, they encountered heavy rains and greatly swollen waters.
translations.idiomatic: While he was Zhili administration commissioner, the Qianlong Emperor traveled to Rehe; at Miyun torrential rain had swollen the rivers.

sentences.zh: 上欲策騎亂流渡，三寶諫曰：「千金之子，坐不垂堂。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to spur his horse through the turbulent current to cross; San Bao remonstrated: "The son worth a thousand in gold does not sit beneath the eaves of a low hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to ride through the churning current; San Bao remonstrated: "A man of priceless worth does not court danger under a crumbling eave.

sentences.zh: 今以萬乘輕狎波濤，使禦駟有失，臣等雖萬段，何可追悔？」

translations.literal: Now, with the ten-thousand-chariot ruler lightly treating the billows, if the imperial steeds should come to harm, though your servants be torn in ten thousand pieces, how could regret be undone?"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty, lord of ten thousand chariots, treats the flood lightly and the imperial horses come to grief, though we servants be torn limb from limb, what remedy would there be?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「滿洲舊俗宜親習勞勚，顧不可耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "By Manchu custom one should personally accustom oneself to toil—may that not be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Manchu custom calls for sharing hardship firsthand—surely that is fitting?"

sentences.zh: 三寶復曰：「上方奉太后乘輿同臨幸，即上渡河安便，不識奉太后何所？」

translations.literal: San Bao replied again: "Your Majesty is now accompanying the empress dowager's carriage on this tour; even if crossing the river is convenient for Your Majesty, where would the empress dowager be placed?"
translations.idiomatic: San Bao replied: "Your Majesty is traveling with the empress dowager's carriage; even if the crossing is safe for you, how is the empress dowager to cross?"

sentences.zh: 上動容，為之回轡。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and turned his horse back for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and turned his horse back.

sentences.zh: 其為上書房總師傅，輯古今儲貳事曰春華日覽，授諸皇子，論者謂其得師保之體云。

translations.literal: As chief tutor of the Upper Study he compiled affairs of heirs apparent ancient and modern into Spring Splendor Daily Perusal and presented it to the princes; commentators said he had grasped the substance of a tutor and guardian.
translations.idiomatic: As chief tutor of the Upper Study he compiled a digest of crown-prince affairs through the ages, entitled Spring Splendor Daily Perusal, for the imperial sons; critics said he embodied the true role of tutor and guardian.

sentences.zh: 永貴，字心齋，拜都氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Yong Gui, style Xinzhaī, of the Baidu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gui, styled Xinzhaī, of the Baidu clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父布蘭泰，自云騎尉世職授理籓院員外郎。

translations.literal: His father Bulantai, from a hereditary yunqiwei post, was appointed an assistant department director in the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bulantai entered service from a hereditary yunqiwei post as an assistant director in the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，為江西巡撫，治嚴刻，世宗召還京師面詰之，對曰：「臣治事從嚴，待上改正，俾恩出自上。」

translations.literal: During the Yongzheng reign, as Jiangxi governor his rule was harsh; the Shizong Emperor summoned him back to the capital to question him face to face, and he replied: "Your servant governs strictly, awaiting Your Majesty's correction so that grace may issue from above."
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng, as Jiangxi governor he ruled harshly; the Yongzheng Emperor recalled him to Beijing and questioned him in person. He answered: "I govern strictly so that Your Majesty may temper my excesses and bestow mercy yourself."

sentences.zh: 世宗不懌，奪職。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor was displeased and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng was displeased and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 尋復起，至古北口提督。

translations.literal: He was soon reappointed and rose to provincial military commander at Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reinstated and eventually became provincial military commander at Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡愨僖。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Mìnxī.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Mìnxī (Sincere and Joyful).

sentences.zh: 永貴，自筆帖式授戶部主事。

translations.literal: Yong Gui, from a clerk's post, was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gui rose from a clerkship to a secretaryship in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: Early in the Qianlong reign he was promoted step by step to director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong he was promoted through several ranks to director.

sentences.zh: 出為湖南辰沅永靖道。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Hunan Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as intendant of the Hunan Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 擢雲南布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Yunnan provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to Yunnan provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 移浙江，署巡撫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhejiang and served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Zhejiang as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 前總督李衛領鹽政，發帑收馀鹽，名曰「帑鹽」；

translations.literal: The former governor-general Li Wei had overseen the salt administration, disbursing treasury funds to purchase surplus salt, called "treasury salt";
translations.idiomatic: Former governor-general Li Wei had run the salt monopoly, using treasury funds to buy surplus salt under the name "treasury salt";

sentences.zh: 令武職任緝私，其制未善。

translations.literal: military officers were charged with suppressing smuggling, and the system was not sound.
translations.idiomatic: military officers were assigned to suppress smuggling—a system that had proved unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 永貴條上八事，俾文武互任其責，下部議行。

translations.literal: Yong Gui submitted eight detailed proposals so that civil and military officials would share responsibilities; the ministry deliberated and implemented them.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gui submitted eight reform articles dividing duties between civil and military officials; the ministries approved and enacted them.

sentences.zh: 居三年，命真除。

translations.literal: After three years he was ordered to receive formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he received a regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 溫、台諸縣旱，永貴令知府金洪銓治賑，不稱職。

translations.literal: Wenzhou, Taizhou, and other counties suffered drought; Yong Gui ordered Prefect Jin Hongquan to manage relief, but he was incompetent.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck Wenzhou, Taizhou, and neighboring counties, Yong Gui put Prefect Jin Hongquan in charge of relief, but Jin proved inadequate.

sentences.zh: 永貴論劾，請休致。

translations.literal: Yong Gui memorialized in impeachment and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gui impeached him and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 總督喀爾吉善再劾，上為奪洪銓職。

translations.literal: Governor-General Ka'erjishan impeached again; the emperor stripped Hongquan of office on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Ka'erjishan joined the impeachment, and the emperor dismissed Hongquan.

sentences.zh: 御史範廷楷因劾永貴瞻徇，上難其代，命寬之。

translations.literal: Censor Fan Tingkai thereupon impeached Yong Gui for favoritism; the emperor found it hard to replace him and ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fan Tingkai then impeached Yong Gui for partiality; the emperor was reluctant to replace him and ordered the matter set aside.

sentences.zh: 永貴請留本省及江蘇漕八十萬，借撥江蘇等省米五十五萬，又請開事例，補倉儲。

translations.literal: Yong Gui requested retaining eight hundred thousand piculs of grain tribute in the province and Jiangsu, borrowing and allocating five hundred fifty thousand piculs of grain from Jiangsu and other provinces, and also requested opening a sale of offices to replenish granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gui asked to retain eight hundred thousand piculs of local and Jiangsu tribute grain, borrow five hundred fifty thousand piculs from Jiangsu and other provinces, and open a sale-of-offices drive to refill the granaries.

sentences.zh: 上責其張皇，既又聞永貴陳災狀有所諱飾，乃命奪職，赴北路軍董理糧餉。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached him for alarmism; then, hearing that Yong Gui's reports on the disaster had been concealed and embellished, he ordered dismissal and sent him to the northern-route army to oversee grain and pay.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for exaggeration; learning later that Yong Gui had glossed over the disaster reports, he stripped him of office and sent him to manage provisions on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 居三年，賜按察使銜，署甘肅臨洮道，仍赴巴里坤主餉。

translations.literal: After three years he was granted the rank of provincial surveillance commissioner and acted as Gansu Lintao Circuit intendant, still going to Barkol to oversee provisions.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was given surveillance-commissioner rank, acted as Gansu Lintao intendant, and continued to manage supplies at Barkol.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，加副都統銜，兼參贊大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was given vice commander's rank and served concurrently as assisting grand minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 21 he received vice commander's rank and was made an assisting grand minister.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬，厄魯特宰桑達什策淩等為亂，定邊右副將軍兆惠駐伊犁辦賊。

translations.literal: That winter the Oirat zaisang Dashiceling and others rebelled; the Pacification Commissioner on the Right, Deputy General Zhaohui, was stationed at Ili to handle the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Oirat chief Dashiceling and others rose in revolt; Deputy General Zhaohui was posted at Ili to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 永貴既抵巴里坤，具以軍事上聞，上嘉其奮勉，予三等輕車都尉世職，令從兆惠自額林沁畢爾罕進兵。

translations.literal: When Yong Gui reached Barkol he reported fully on military affairs; the emperor praised his exertions, granted a hereditary third-rank commandery chariot captaincy, and ordered him to follow Zhaohui in advancing from Elinqin Bi'erhan.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Barkol Yong Gui reported fully on the campaign; the emperor commended his zeal, granted a hereditary third-rank commandery chariot captaincy, and ordered him to advance with Zhaohui from Elinqin Bi'erhan.

sentences.zh: 命署西安巡撫，未之任，令赴魯克察克屯田。

translations.literal: He was ordered to act as Xi'an governor but did not take up the post and was sent to Lukchak to open military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was named acting Xi'an governor but never assumed the post and was sent to establish military farms at Lukchak.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以侍郎銜留軍，因授刑部侍郎，董屯田。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, with vice-minister's rank he remained with the army; he was then appointed Vice Minister of Justice and supervised military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 23 he stayed with the army as a vice-minister and was appointed Vice Minister of Justice to oversee the colony program.

sentences.zh: 烏魯木齊、闢展、托克三、哈喇沙爾、昌吉、羅克倫皆駐兵營墾，秋穫得穀三萬五千八百馀石。

translations.literal: At Urumqi, Kuche, Toksan, Karashahr, Changji, and Luokelun garrison farms were all established; the autumn harvest yielded more than thirty-five thousand eight hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison colonies were opened at Urumqi, Kuche, Toksan, Karashahr, Changji, and Luokelun, yielding over thirty-five thousand eight hundred piculs in the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 是時兆惠兵次葉爾羌，命永貴駐阿克蘇主餽軍。

translations.literal: At that time Zhaohui's army was at Yarkand; Yong Gui was ordered to remain at Aksu to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaohui's forces were then at Yarkand; Yong Gui was stationed at Aksu to provision the campaign.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，還至庫車，布政使德舒為嗎哈沁所戕。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he returned to Kucha; the administration commissioner Deshu was killed by Mahakin.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 24 he returned to Kucha, where administration commissioner Deshu was murdered by Mahakin rebels.

sentences.zh: 永貴與護軍統領努三協殲逆眾，回部平。

translations.literal: Yong Gui, together with garrison commander Nu San, jointly exterminated the rebels, and the Muslim regions were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gui and garrison commander Nu San jointly destroyed the rebels, pacifying the Muslim territories.

sentences.zh: 移倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Vice Minister of the Granary Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of the Granary Directorate.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，命赴克什噶爾辦事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was ordered to go to Kashgar to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 26 he was sent to serve as Kashgar commissioner.

sentences.zh: 旋授禮部尚書、鑲紅旗漢軍都統，仍駐克什噶爾。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Minister of Rites and commander of the Bordered Red Banner Chinese Martial Force, still stationed at Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of Rites and commander of the Bordered Red Banner Chinese Martial Force while remaining at Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 疏請疏溝渠，興耕稼，議自赫色勒河東南浚渠四十馀裡，引水入赫色勒布伊，材托庸河湍急，宜增堤壩，鑿山石，弱水勢。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting dredging of canals and promotion of agriculture, proposing to dredge a canal of more than forty li southeast from the Hesele River to draw water into Hesele Buyi; the Cai Tuoyong River ran swift and steep, where dikes and dams should be increased, mountain stone cut, and the water's force weakened.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for canal dredging and expanded farming, proposing a canal of over forty li southeast from the Hesele River to irrigate Hesele Buyi; where the swift Cai Tuoyong River ran steep, he urged higher dikes, stone cutting, and measures to reduce the current.

sentences.zh: 召還京師。

translations.literal: He was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 三十年，烏什回人為亂，復命赴哈什哈爾。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the Ush Muslims rebelled; he was again ordered to go to Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 30, when the Muslims of Ush rebelled, he was again sent to Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 事平，移駐烏什。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he moved his station to Ush.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed he was stationed at Ush.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，署伊犁將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he acted as Ili general.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 33 he served as acting Ili general.

sentences.zh: 移吏部，再移禮部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, then again to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Ministry of Personnel and then back to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 坐厄魯特兵盜哈薩克馬轉誣哈薩克，辦事大臣巴爾品斷獄未得其實，永貴論劾，語有所諉飾。

translations.literal: He was implicated because Oirat soldiers stole Kazakh horses and then falsely accused the Kazakhs; the frontier commissioner Ba'erpin's judgment did not get at the facts, and Yong Gui's impeachment memorial contained language of evasion and embellishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was faulted when Oirat troops stole Kazakh horses and shifted blame to the Kazakhs; frontier commissioner Ba'erpin's ruling missed the truth, and Yong Gui's impeachment used evasive language.

sentences.zh: 又以涼州、莊浪滿洲兵損馬當償，誤扣熱河兵餉，召還京師，命授左都御史，命不得用翎頂。

translations.literal: Also, because Liangzhou and Zhuanglang Manchu troops' lost horses were to be compensated, he mistakenly withheld Rehe troops' pay; recalled to the capital, he was ordered appointed Left Censor-in-Chief but forbidden to wear the peacock feather and ruby finial.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrongly docked Rehe troop pay to cover horse losses among Liangzhou and Zhuanglang Manchu garrisons; recalled to Beijing, he was made Left Censor-in-Chief but stripped of peacock feather and finial privileges.

sentences.zh: 旋移禮部尚書，得用頂帶，仍不得戴翎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Minister of Rites, permitted to use the finial cap, but still not allowed to wear the feather.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Minister of Rites, allowed his finial cap again, but still denied the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，命署大學士，題孝聖憲皇后神主。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was ordered to act as Grand Secretary and to inscribe the spirit tablet of Empress Xiaoshengxian.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 42 he was named acting Grand Secretary and charged with inscribing the spirit tablet of Empress Xiaoshengxian.

sentences.zh: 尋補吏部尚書，在阿哥總諳達處行走，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made Minister of Personnel, served on duty in the princes' chief instructorship, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of Personnel, assigned to the princes' chief instructorship, and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 初，山東民王倫為亂，給事中李漱芳陳奏饑民釀釁，坐妄言，左授禮部主事。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Shandong commoner Wang Lun rebelled, Supervising Secretary Li Shufang memorialized that famine victims were brewing trouble; for reckless speech he was demoted to a secretaryship in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Lun of Shandong rose in rebellion, Supervising Secretary Li Shufang had warned that famine victims were brewing unrest; he was demoted to a Rites Ministry secretary for what was judged reckless speech.

sentences.zh: 及是，吏部請以漱芳升授員外郎。

translations.literal: At this time the Ministry of Personnel requested promoting Shufang to assistant department director.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Ministry of Personnel proposed promoting Shufang to assistant department director.

sentences.zh: 上責永貴市恩，削職奪花翎，令以三品頂帶赴烏什辦事。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Yong Gui for currying favor, stripped his office and took back the peacock feather, and ordered him to go to Ush to handle affairs with a third-rank finial cap.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused Yong Gui of trading favors, stripped his rank and peacock feather, and sent him to Ush with a third-rank cap.

sentences.zh: 詔詰責甚至，且言：「永貴回烏什，如不實心任事，必在彼處正法。」

translations.literal: The edict rebuked him severely, saying: "If Yong Gui returns to Ush and does not serve in earnest, he will certainly be executed on the spot there."
translations.idiomatic: The edict rebuked him harshly, declaring: "If Yong Gui returns to Ush and does not serve wholeheartedly, he will be executed there."

sentences.zh: 先是葉爾羌辦事大臣侍郎高樸役回民采玉，並婪取金珠，為諸伯克所訟。

translations.literal: Earlier the Yarkand frontier commissioner, Vice Minister Gao Pu, had forced Muslim commoners to gather jade and had greedily taken gold and gems, and was sued by the begs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yarkand commissioner Gao Pu had forced Muslim subjects to mine jade and extorted gold and gems, provoking lawsuits from the local begs.

sentences.zh: 永貴如葉爾羌，訊得實，聞上。

translations.literal: Yong Gui went to Yarkand, investigated and found the facts true, and reported to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gui went to Yarkand, confirmed the charges, and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上為誅高樸，手詔嘉永貴持正，並謂：「永貴罪不至貶。

translations.literal: The emperor had Gao Pu executed, and in a personal edict praised Yong Gui for uprightness, also saying: "Yong Gui's offense did not warrant demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor executed Gao Pu and wrote personally to praise Yong Gui's integrity, adding: "Yong Gui's offense did not warrant demotion.

sentences.zh: 今命西行，適以發高樸之姦，潛銷禍萌，此天啟朕衷也！」

translations.literal: Now, ordering him westward, it happened to expose Gao Pu's wickedness and quietly remove the sprout of disaster—this is Heaven opening My mind!"
translations.idiomatic: Sending him west now exposed Gao Pu's crimes and quietly removed a growing threat—Heaven has guided My purpose!"

sentences.zh: 仍授吏部尚書，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Minister of Personnel and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed Minister of Personnel and given back the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 尋授參贊大臣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed assisting grand minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made an assisting grand minister.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，召還京師，授鑲藍旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was recalled to the capital and appointed commander of the Bordered Blue Banner Manchu force.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 44 he was recalled to Beijing and made commander of the Bordered Blue Banner Manchus.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was made associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 45 he became associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，卒，諡文勤。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he died and was given the posthumous title Wénqín.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 48 he died and was posthumously titled Wénqín (Cultivated and Diligent).

sentences.zh: 永貴端謹。

translations.literal: Yong Gui was upright and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gui was upright and conscientious.

sentences.zh: 初直軍機處，與阿桂齊名，時稱「二桂」。

translations.literal: Early on he served in the Grand Council and was as famous as Agui; at the time they were called "the two Guis."
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career he served in the Grand Council alongside Agui; the pair were known as "the two Guis."

sentences.zh: 其撫浙江，有廉聲。

translations.literal: In governing Zhejiang he had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhejiang governor he earned a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 子 伊江阿 子伊江阿，官至山東巡撫。

translations.literal: Son: Yijiang'a. His son Yijiang'a rose to governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yijiang'a. His son Yijiang'a rose to governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，伊江阿因奏事附書和珅勸節哀。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor died, Yijiang'a, in a routine memorial, enclosed a letter urging Heshen to moderate his grief.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qianlong Emperor's death, Yijiang'a attached to a routine memorial a note urging Heshen to moderate his mourning.

sentences.zh: 和□申已下獄，仁宗得其書，詔詰責，奪職。

translations.literal: Heshen was already imprisoned; the Renzong Emperor obtained the letter, issued an edict of stern rebuke, and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen was already in prison; the Jiaqing Emperor obtained the letter, rebuked him by edict, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 既，又追論在山東日佞佛寬盜，命戍伊犁。

translations.literal: Afterward he was again prosecuted for flattering Buddhism and being lenient toward bandits during his days in Shandong, and was ordered exiled to Ili.
translations.idiomatic: He was later prosecuted for promoting Buddhism and being lenient toward bandits while in Shandong and was banished to Ili.

sentences.zh: 尋授藍翎侍衛、古城領隊大臣。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed a blue-lance guardsman and commandant at Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a blue-lance guardsman and frontier commandant at Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 蔡新，字次明，福建漳浦人，贈尚書世遠族子。

translations.literal: Cai Xin, style Ciming, was a native of Zhangpu, Fujian, and a clansman of the posthumously honored Minister Shi Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xin, styled Ciming, came from Zhangpu in Fujian and was a kinsman of the posthumously honored Minister Shi Yuan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned jinshi in Qianlong 1 (1736), entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 入直上書房。

translations.literal: He entered service in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 試御史第一，辭，授侍講。

translations.literal: He ranked first in the censor examination but declined and was appointed expositor.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the censor examination but declined the post and was made an expositor.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部侍郎，移刑部。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to Vice Minister of Works, then transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several ranks to Vice Minister of Works and was then moved to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以母老請歸省，賜其母貂緞；

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, because his mother was aged he requested leave to return home to visit her, and sable fur was bestowed on his mother;
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 18 he asked leave to visit his elderly mother and the court bestowed sable fur on her;

sentences.zh: 旋乞終養，允之。

translations.literal: he then begged to retire permanently to care for her, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: he then asked to retire permanently to care for her, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 即家命為上書房總師傅，辭，高宗諭之曰：「非令汝即來供職，待後日耳。」

translations.literal: While at home he was ordered to be chief tutor of the Upper Study; he declined, and the Gaozong Emperor instructed him: "This is not ordering you to come immediately to serve; it is for a later day."
translations.idiomatic: At home he was named chief tutor of the Upper Study but declined; the Qianlong Emperor told him: "I am not asking you to take up duty at once—only for some later day."

sentences.zh: 二十五年，上五十壽，入京師祝嘏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, when the emperor reached fifty, he entered the capital to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 25, for the emperor's fiftieth birthday, he went to Beijing to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，南巡，覲行在。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, on the southern tour, he had an audience at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 26 he had an audience with the emperor during the southern tour.

sentences.zh: 母喪終，授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When his mourning for his mother ended, he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning period he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 32 he was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，移禮部。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 38 he was moved to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，命以吏部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was ordered to serve as associate Grand Secretary while Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 45 he was made associate Grand Secretary while retaining the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，乞假修墓。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he begged leave to repair tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 46 he took leave to repair family tombs.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，還朝。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 48 he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 拜文華殿大學士，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Wenhua Hall Grand Secretary and concurrently Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Wenhua Hall Grand Secretary and concurrent Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 五十年，與千叟宴。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he attended the banquet of a thousand elders.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 50 he attended the banquet of a thousand elders.

sentences.zh: 上臨雍講學，新以大學士領國子監，講易「天行健，君子以自強不息」，賜茶並文綺。

translations.literal: When the emperor lectured at the Imperial Academy, Xin, as Grand Secretary heading the Directorate of Education, lectured on the Changes: "Heaven moves with strength; the noble man thereby strengthens himself without ceasing," and was granted tea and patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor lectured at the Imperial Academy, Xin, as Grand Secretary and head of the Directorate of Education, expounded the line "Heaven moves with strength; the noble man strengthens himself without ceasing" and received tea and brocade.

sentences.zh: 新操履端謹，言行必衷於禮法。

translations.literal: Xin's conduct was upright and cautious; in word and deed he always adhered to ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was upright and cautious, and his words and deeds always conformed to ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 上眷之厚，賦臨雍詩，注謂：「今群臣孰可當三老五更？

translations.literal: The emperor favored him deeply; in a poem on lecturing at the Academy he noted: "Among the ministers today, who could serve as the Three Elders and Five Geng?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored him deeply; in a poem on the Academy lecture he wrote: "Which minister today could serve as the Three Elders and Five Geng?

sentences.zh: 獨新長朕四歲，或可居兄事。

translations.literal: Only Xin is four years older than I and might be treated as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xin is four years my senior and might be treated as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 然恐其局促勿敢當，舉王導對晉元帝語以謝耳。」

translations.literal: Yet I fear he would be constrained and not dare accept, and would cite Wang Dao's reply to Emperor Yuan of Jin in declining."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear he would be too modest to accept and would cite Wang Dao's reply to Emperor Yuan of Jin in declining."

sentences.zh: 新上疏乞致仕，語切至，上許其歸，加太子太師，三賦詩以餞。

translations.literal: Xin memorialized begging to retire; his words were earnest, and the emperor permitted his return, adding the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and composing three poems to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: Xin memorialized to retire in earnest terms; the emperor allowed him to go home, made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and composed three farewell poems.

sentences.zh: 既歸，上每製文，屢以寄新，且曰：「在朝無可與言古文者。

translations.literal: After his return, whenever the emperor composed writings he often sent them to Xin, saying: "At court there is no one with whom to discuss ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: After he retired, the emperor often sent him new compositions, saying: "At court there is no one with whom I can discuss classical prose.

sentences.zh: 不可阿好徒稱頌。」

translations.literal: You must not flatter me with empty praise."
translations.idiomatic: Do not flatter me with empty praise."

sentences.zh: 五十五年，上八十壽，詣京師祝嘏，賜宴同樂園，賜人葠一斤。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, when the emperor reached eighty, he went to the capital to offer congratulations, was feasted at the Garden of Shared Joy, and granted one jin of ginseng.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 55, for the emperor's eightieth birthday, he went to Beijing to congratulate him, was feasted at the Garden of Shared Joy, and received one jin of ginseng.

sentences.zh: 及歸，命歸途所經，有司具舟車護行。

translations.literal: On his return he was ordered that along the route local officials should provide boats and carriages to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return journey local officials along the route were ordered to provide boats and carriages as an escort.

sentences.zh: 上仍以詩文寄新，諭將以驗學詣，戒詩毋和韻。

translations.literal: The emperor still sent poems and essays to Xin, instructing that when he came to test his learning he should not compose matching-rhyme poems.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor continued sending him poems and essays, telling him that when he came to demonstrate his learning he should not write matching-rhyme verse.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，重赴鹿鳴宴。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he again attended the Deer Call banquet.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 57 he again attended the Deer Call banquet.

sentences.zh: 六十年，上御極六十載，諭新不必入賀。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, when the emperor had reigned sixty years, he instructed Xin that he need not come to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 60, when the emperor marked sixty years on the throne, he told Xin he need not come to court to congratulate him.

sentences.zh: 新奏言上九旬萬壽，冀再詣闕祝嘏。

translations.literal: Xin memorialized that when the emperor reached ninety he hoped to come again to the palace to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Xin memorialized that he hoped to come to court again when the emperor reached ninety.

sentences.zh: 上諭之曰：「覽奏，字字出誠心，我君臣共勉之。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him: "Having read your memorial, every word comes from sincerity; let us ruler and minister encourage one another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Every word of your memorial speaks from the heart; let us encourage one another as ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 若天恩得符所原，實佳話也！」

translations.literal: If Heaven's grace fulfills your wish, it will truly be a fine story!"
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven grants your wish, it will be a fine story indeed!"

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，新年九十，賜額曰「綠野恆春」​​，侑以諸珍物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, when Xin reached ninety, he was granted an inscription reading "Evergreen in the Green Fields," together with many precious objects.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1, when Xin turned ninety, the court bestowed the plaque "Evergreen in the Green Fields" along with many precious gifts.

sentences.zh: 四年，高宗崩，奔赴，至福州，病不能進。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the Gaozong Emperor died, he hurried to attend but reached Fuzhou and, ill, could not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4, when the Qianlong Emperor died, he set out to attend the mourning but fell ill at Fuzhou and could go no farther.

sentences.zh: 巡撫汪志伊以聞，溫詔止其行。

translations.literal: Governor Wang Zhiyi reported this, and a warm edict ordered him to stop his journey.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Zhiyi reported his condition, and a gracious edict told him to turn back.

sentences.zh: 是冬，卒，贈太傅，諡文端。

translations.literal: That winter he died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor, with the title Wénduān.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the title Wénduān (Cultivated and Steady).

sentences.zh: 新學以求仁為宗，以不動心為要。

translations.literal: Xin's learning took seeking benevolence as its aim and an unmoved mind as its essential point.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's learning aimed at benevolence and prized an unmoved mind.

sentences.zh: 嘗輯先儒操心、養心、存心、求放心諸語，曰事心錄。

translations.literal: He once compiled sayings of earlier Confucians on tending the mind, nourishing the mind, preserving the mind, and recovering the lost mind, entitled Records of Mind-Cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled earlier Confucian teachings on mind-cultivation into Records of Mind-Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 直上書房四十二年，培養啟迪，動必稱儒先。

translations.literal: In the Upper Study for forty-two years he nurtured and enlightened, always invoking the sages of old in his teaching.
translations.idiomatic: For forty-two years in the Upper Study he nurtured the princes, always invoking the sages of old.

sentences.zh: 高宗以新究心根柢，守世遠家法，深敬禮之。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor, because Xin had penetrated the roots of the mind and kept the family tradition of Shi Yuan, deeply honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong deeply honored him for his mastery of moral foundations and for upholding the family tradition of Shi Yuan.

sentences.zh: 既歸，福建督撫坐貪黷、虧倉庫得重譴，上責「新知而不言，自比寒蟬，無體國公忠之意」。

translations.literal: After his return, the Fujian governor-general and governor were heavily punished for corruption and granary deficits; the emperor reproached Xin: "You knew but did not speak, likening yourself to a winter cicada, without the spirit of serving the state with public loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: After he retired, Fujian's top officials were heavily punished for corruption and granary shortfalls; the emperor rebuked Xin: "You knew but kept silent, like a winter cicada—where was your loyalty to the state?"

sentences.zh: 新上疏請下吏議，卒以篤老寬之。

translations.literal: Xin memorialized asking to be handed over to the officials for judgment; in the end he was leniently treated on account of his great age.
translations.idiomatic: Xin asked to be handed over for official judgment; in the end his great age won him leniency.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，海盜方肆，新子本俊官京師，御史宋樹疏言新家書及海盜事，不以聞。

translations.literal: Early in Jiaqing, when pirates were rampant, Xin's son Benjun held office in the capital; Censor Song Shu memorialized that family letters from Xin concerning pirates had not been reported.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaqing, when pirates were rampant, Xin's son Benjun served in Beijing; Censor Song Shu charged that family letters from Xin about piracy had not been reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上為詰本俊，本俊言新已具疏令謄真入奏，上亦不之責，仍諭新毋畏。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Benjun; Benjun said Xin had already prepared a memorial and ordered a fair copy for submission; the emperor did not blame him and still instructed Xin not to fear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Benjun, who said Xin had already drafted a memorial for submission; the emperor did not blame him and told Xin not to be afraid.

sentences.zh: 新家居謙慎，遇丞尉執禮必恭。

translations.literal: At home Xin was humble and cautious; when he met assistant magistrates and constables he always observed ritual with respect.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he was humble; he always treated local magistrates and constables with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 或問之，曰：「欲使鄉人知位至宰相，亦必敬本籍官吏，庶心有所不敢，犯法者鮮耳。」

translations.literal: When asked, he said: "I wish the people of my district to know that even one who reaches the rank of chief minister must still respect the officials of his native place, so that in their hearts they will not dare, and lawbreakers will be few."
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, he said: "I want my neighbors to see that even a chief minister must respect local officials, so they will think twice before breaking the law."

sentences.zh: 著有緝齋詩文集。

translations.literal: He authored the Jizhai collected poems and essays.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Jizhai collected poems and essays.

sentences.zh: 程景伊，字聘三，江南武進人。

translations.literal: Cheng Jingyi, style Pingsan, was a native of Wujin in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jingyi, styled Pingsan, came from Wujin in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned jinshi in Qianlong 4 (1739), entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 再遷侍讀學士，命在上書房行走。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to reader of the Hanlin Academy and ordered to serve on duty in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin reader and assigned to the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 復三遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: After three more promotions he became Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After three further promotions he became Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 景伊致人書，言：「承乏中樞，晨夕內廷多曠廢。

translations.literal: Jingyi sent someone a letter saying: "Holding a post at the center, morning and evening in the inner court much is neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi wrote to an acquaintance: "Holding a central post, I neglect my duties morning and evening in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 今秋未與木蘭之役，稍得專心職業。」

translations.literal: This autumn I did not join the Mulan hunt and can somewhat concentrate on my duties."
translations.idiomatic: This autumn I missed the Mulan hunt and can finally focus on my work."

sentences.zh: 為上聞，責其躭逸，解上書房行走。

translations.literal: This came to the emperor's ears; he reproached him for indulgence in ease and relieved him of duty in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it, rebuked him for idleness, and removed him from the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 歷禮、工諸部。

translations.literal: He served in the Ministries of Rites and Works among others.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Ministries of Rites and Works among others.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，擢工部尚書，歷刑、吏諸部。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was promoted to Minister of Works and passed through the Ministries of Justice and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 34 he was made Minister of Works and later served in the Ministries of Justice and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was made associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 38 he became associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，上東巡迴鑾，駐蹕黃新莊。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year the emperor made an eastern tour and returned; halting at Huangxinzhuang,
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 41, on the emperor's return from an eastern tour, the court halted at Huangxinzhuang.

sentences.zh: 景伊與在京王大臣迎駕，未召見即退班，命奪職，仍留任。

translations.literal: Jingyi, together with princes and grand ministers in the capital who welcomed the imperial carriage, withdrew from attendance before being summoned; he was ordered stripped of office but still retained in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi joined the Beijing princes and ministers in welcoming the emperor but left before being received; he was stripped of rank but kept in office.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，授文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was appointed Wenyuan Pavilion Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 44 he was made Wenyuan Pavilion Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，上南巡，命景伊留京治事。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, on the southern tour, he was ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 45, during the southern tour, he was left in Beijing to manage affairs.

sentences.zh: 上還京師，入對，以景伊病後衰弱，命安心調理，勿勉強行走。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital and Jingyi had an audience, because Jingyi was weak after illness he was ordered to rest and recuperate in peace and not force himself to walk.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, Jingyi had an audience; finding him weak after illness, the emperor told him to rest and not force himself to walk.

sentences.zh: 七月，卒，諡文恭。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he died and was given the posthumous title Wéngōng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month and was posthumously titled Wéngōng (Cultivated and Respectful).

sentences.zh: 梁國治，字階平，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: Liang Guozhi, style Jieping, was a native of Kuaiji, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Guozhi, styled Jieping, came from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination as top graduate of the first class and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13 (1748) he took first place in the jinshi examination and was appointed a reviser.

sentences.zh: 遷國子監司業。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be vice director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 充廣東鄉試正考官。

translations.literal: He served as chief examiner of the Guangdong provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief examiner of the Guangdong provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 復命，奏對稱旨，命以道員發廣東待缺。

translations.literal: On reporting back, his audience responses pleased the emperor, and he was ordered dispatched to Guangdong as a circuit intendant awaiting a vacancy.
translations.idiomatic: On reporting back, his audience pleased the emperor, who sent him to Guangdong as a circuit intendant awaiting appointment.

sentences.zh: 旋除惠嘉潮道，移署糧驛道。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed to the Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jieyang Circuit and then transferred to act as grain and courier intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to the Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jieyang Circuit and then acted as grain and courier intendant.

sentences.zh: 卓異引見，擢署左副都御史。

translations.literal: Cited for outstanding merit and presented to the throne, he was promoted to act as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Cited for outstanding merit, he was promoted to acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 廣東總督楊廷璋等追論國治署糧驛道時失察家人舞弊，讞實，奪職。

translations.literal: Guangdong Governor-General Yang Tingzhang and others pursued the case that when Guozhi acted as grain and courier intendant he failed to detect household servants' fraud; the judgment was confirmed and he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong Governor-General Yang Tingzhang prosecuted him for failing to detect household fraud while acting as grain intendant; the charge was sustained and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 起授山西冀寧道。

translations.literal: He was reappointed and made Shanxi Jining Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was reinstated as Shanxi Jining Circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 三遷湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，命署湖廣總督，兼荊州將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was ordered to act as governor-general of Huguang and concurrently as Jingzhou general.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 34 he was named acting Huguang governor-general and concurrent Jingzhou general.

sentences.zh: 時湖北頻歲水旱，治賑，缺倉穀四十八萬馀石。

translations.literal: At that time Hubei had floods and droughts in successive years; in managing relief the granaries were short by more than four hundred eighty thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei had suffered repeated floods and droughts; relief efforts left granaries short by over four hundred eighty thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 國治議發司庫白金二十萬，俟秋穫易穀，來歲春夏間出糶，石溢銀一錢。

translations.literal: Guozhi proposed disbursing two hundred thousand taels of treasury silver from the provincial treasury, waiting until the autumn harvest to exchange for grain, then in the spring and summer of the coming year selling grain, with one tael profit per picul.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhi proposed releasing two hundred thousand taels from the provincial treasury to buy grain after the autumn harvest and sell it the following spring and summer at one tael profit per picul.

sentences.zh: 行之數年，倉穀得無缺。

translations.literal: Carried out for several years, the granaries were kept without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: After several years the granaries were kept full.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，移湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was transferred to governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 36 he was moved to Hunan governor.

sentences.zh: 師徵金川，治軍械，造藥彈，費不給。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against Jinchuan, he managed military equipment and manufactured gunpowder and shells, but funds were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinchuan campaign he supplied arms and ammunition, but funds ran short.

sentences.zh: 國治請以司庫儲備軍興白金十馀萬，照一年應扣各糧通行借給，仍分三年扣還歸款。

translations.literal: Guozhi requested using more than one hundred thousand taels of treasury silver reserved for military expenses, lending it broadly according to each year's grain deductions, to be repaid in installments over three years.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhi asked to lend over one hundred thousand taels from military reserves, advancing it against annual grain quotas to be repaid over three years.

sentences.zh: 國治又以出征將弁，例軍中升用，本營缺出，仍系照常拔補。

translations.literal: Guozhi also noted that for officers on campaign, promotion was customarily made in the army, while vacancies in their home camps were still filled by routine selection.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhi also noted that officers on campaign were promoted in the field while home-camp vacancies were filled by routine seniority.

sentences.zh: 循資按格者，轉得坐致升遷；

translations.literal: those who advanced by seniority and qualification could sit and obtain promotion;
translations.idiomatic: Those who advanced by seniority could gain promotion without fighting;

sentences.zh: 冒敵衝鋒者，專待軍營缺出，無以鼓勵戎行。

translations.literal: while those who braved the enemy in the charge had only to wait for army vacancies, giving no encouragement to military service.
translations.idiomatic: while men who charged the enemy had to wait for field vacancies—giving little incentive to valor.

sentences.zh: 請嗣後本營缺出，與出征將弁一體論升。

translations.literal: He requested that thereafter home-camp vacancies and officers on campaign be considered together for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that home-camp vacancies and campaign officers be considered together for promotion.

sentences.zh: 皆從其請。

translations.literal: All his requests were granted.
translations.idiomatic: All his proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，召還京師，命在軍機處行走，並直南書房。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was recalled to the capital, ordered to serve on duty in the Grand Council, and also assigned to the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 38 he was recalled to Beijing, assigned to the Grand Council, and also to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，授戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 39 he was made Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，遷尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was transferred to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 42 he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，加太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was given the additional title Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 47 he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，命協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was ordered to serve as associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 48 he was made associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 五十年，晉授東閣大學士，兼戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he was advanced to Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary and concurrently Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 50 he was promoted to Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary and concurrent Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，卒，加太子太保，諡文定。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he died; he was given the additional title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Wéndìng.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 51 he died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with the title Wéndìng (Cultivated and Settled).

sentences.zh: 國治父文標，官刑部司獄，卹囚有惠政。

translations.literal: Guozhi's father Wenbiao served as a jailer in the Ministry of Justice and showed compassionate policy toward prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhi's father Wenbiao was a jailer in the Ministry of Justice known for humane treatment of prisoners.

sentences.zh: 國治篤孝友，與兄孿生，兄蚤卒，終生不稱壽，事嫂如母。

translations.literal: Guozhi was deeply filial and brotherly; he and his elder brother were twins; the brother died early, and all his life he never spoke of longevity, treating his sister-in-law as a mother.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhi was deeply filial; his twin brother died young, and he never celebrated his own birthday, treating his sister-in-law as his mother.

sentences.zh: 治事敬慎縝密。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he was reverent, cautious, and meticulous.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was reverent, cautious, and meticulous.

sentences.zh: 生平無疾言遽色，然不可以私幹。

translations.literal: Throughout his life he never spoke harshly or showed sudden anger, yet private requests could not sway him.
translations.idiomatic: He was never harsh or abrupt in manner, yet would not be moved by private appeals.

sentences.zh: 門下士有求入按察使幕主刑名者，戒之曰：「心術不可不慎！」

translations.literal: A follower asked to enter a surveillance commissioner's staff to handle criminal law; he warned him: "One's inner principles must not be treated carelessly!"
translations.idiomatic: When a follower sought a post on a surveillance commissioner's staff handling criminal law, he warned: "You must be scrupulous in your principles!"

sentences.zh: 其人請改治錢穀，則曰：「刑名不慎，不過殺一人，所殺必有數，且為人所共知。

translations.literal: The man asked instead to handle revenue and grain accounts; he said: "If criminal law is handled carelessly, at most one person is killed; the number killed is definite and known to all.
translations.idiomatic: The man asked to handle revenue and grain instead; he said: "Carelessness in criminal law kills at most one person—the toll is finite and public.

sentences.zh: 錢穀厲人，十倍刑名，當時不覺。

translations.literal: Revenue and grain harm people tenfold over criminal law, though at the time one does not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue and grain work harms people ten times more than criminal law, though the harm is not felt at once.

sentences.zh: 近數十年，遠或數百年，流毒至於無窮，且未有已！」

translations.literal: In the near term decades, in the far term perhaps centuries, the poison spreads without end and has not ceased!"
translations.idiomatic: Within decades, or centuries hence, the poison spreads without end and never stops!"

sentences.zh: 卒不許。

translations.literal: In the end he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused.

sentences.zh: 著有敬思堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Jingsi Hall collected works.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Jingsi Hall collected works.

sentences.zh: 英廉，字計六，馮氏，內務府漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Ying Lian, style Jiliu, of the Feng clan, was a Chinese Martial Force bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner in the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Lian, styled Jiliu, of the Feng clan, was a Chinese Martial Force bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner in the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 雍正十年舉人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongzheng he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in Yongzheng 10 (1732).

sentences.zh: 自筆帖式授內務府主事。

translations.literal: From a clerk's post he was appointed a secretary in the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from a clerkship to a secretaryship in the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，命往江南河工學習，補淮安府外河同知。

translations.literal: Early in the Qianlong reign he was ordered to go to Jiangnan to study river works, and was appointed sub-prefect in charge of outer-river works in Huaian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qianlong reign he was sent to Jiangnan to train in river engineering, then appointed sub-prefect for outer-river works in Huaian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累遷永定河道。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became commissioner of the Yongding River.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive postings to commissioner of the Yongding River.

sentences.zh: 河決，總督方觀承劾英廉淤溝鑲埽，衝陷水上月堤，匿不以聞，遂誤要工。

translations.literal: The river breached; Governor-General Fang Guancheng impeached Ying Lian, charging that silted ditches and inset revetments had burst and breached the upper-stage dike above the water line; he concealed this without reporting it, thereby delaying urgent repair work.
translations.idiomatic: When the river breached, Governor-General Fang Guancheng impeached Ying Lian for silt-choked ditches and inset revetments that had burst and collapsed an upstream dike above water level; Ying Lian had kept silent about it, delaying essential repairs.

sentences.zh: 奪職，逮治，英廉抗辨。

translations.literal: His post was stripped, he was arrested for trial, and Ying Lian argued in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of office and taken into custody, Ying Lian contested the charges.

sentences.zh: 逾年讞未決，觀承請遣大臣蒞其事。

translations.literal: More than a year passed without a verdict; Guancheng requested that a high minister be sent to preside over the case.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year without a verdict, Guancheng asked that a senior minister be dispatched to try the case.

sentences.zh: 上命尚書舒赫德會鞫，言英廉申報不以實，且未將淤溝先事預防，堵築經費，當責出私財以償。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Minister Shu Hede to join in the trial; the finding was that Ying Lian's reports had not been truthful, and that he had not taken preventive measures against the silted ditches in advance; the costs of blocking and building works should be recovered from his private funds.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Minister Shu Hede to sit jointly in judgment. The court found that Ying Lian had filed false reports and failed to guard against the silted ditches beforehand; he was to make restitution for blocking and construction costs from his own purse.

sentences.zh: 上諭言：「英廉上官未及兩月，淤溝失防，咎實在前政。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Ying Lian had held office less than two months; the failure to guard the silted ditch—the blame truly lies with the previous administration.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Ying Lian had been in office less than two months; the breach at the silted ditch was really the fault of his predecessor.

sentences.zh: 然觀承以總督劾屬吏，不敢率意入罪，讞逾年未定，請遣大臣蒞其事。

translations.literal: Yet Guancheng, as governor-general impeaching a subordinate, did not dare to convict rashly; the case remained undecided for more than a year, and he requested that a high minister be sent to preside over it.
translations.idiomatic: Still, as governor-general prosecuting a subordinate, Guancheng would not convict lightly; the case dragged on for over a year before he asked for a senior minister to take it over.

sentences.zh: 是其心有所警畏，亦朕明慎庶政之效。

translations.literal: This shows his mind holds some caution and awe; it is also the effect of My clear and careful governance of common affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That shows a salutary fear in his heart—and also the fruit of My own careful stewardship of public affairs.

sentences.zh: 仍從其請。」

translations.literal: His request was still granted."
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted."

sentences.zh: 未幾，命在高樑橋迤西稻田廠效力。

translations.literal: Not long after, he was ordered to serve at the Daotian Farm west of Gaoliang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was ordered to perform menial duty at the Daotian Farm west of Gaoliang Bridge.

sentences.zh: 尋復自筆帖式授內務府主事。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed a secretary in the Imperial Household Department from the rank of clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored from clerk to secretary in the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 累遷內務府正黃旗護軍統領。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became commander of the guards of the Bordered Yellow Banner in the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner guard corps in the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 外授江寧布政使，兼織造。

translations.literal: He was assigned to an external post as financial commissioner of Jiangning, concurrently overseeing textile manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: Posted outside the capital as Jiangning financial commissioner, he also supervised imperial textile production.

sentences.zh: 英廉以父老，乞留京師，賜二品銜，授內務府大臣、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Ying Lian, because his father was old, begged to remain in the capital; he was granted second-rank status and appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Department and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his father's age, Ying Lian asked to stay in Beijing; he was given second-rank honors and made Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Department and Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，徵緬甸，師行，命與尚書托庸等董其事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, when an expedition was launched against Burma and the army marched, he was ordered together with Minister Tuoyong and others to oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 34 (1769), when troops marched against Burma, he was ordered to manage logistics alongside Minister Tuoyong and others.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，仍兼戶部侍郎、正黃旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Punishments, still concurrently holding the posts of Vice Minister of Revenue and commander-in-chief of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of Punishments while retaining his posts as Vice Minister of Revenue and Manchu commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，侍郎高樸劾左都御史觀保，侍郎申保、倪承寬、吳壇交內監高雲從，洩道府記載。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, Vice Minister Gao Pu impeached Censor-in-Chief Guan Bao; Vice Ministers Shen Bao, Ni Chengkuan, and Wu Tan associated with the eunuch Gao Yuncong and leaked circuit and prefectural inspection records.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 39 (1774), Vice Minister Gao Pu impeached Censor-in-Chief Guan Bao, charging that Vice Ministers Shen Bao, Ni Chengkuan, and Wu Tan had dealings with the eunuch Gao Yuncong and leaked provincial inspection records.

sentences.zh: 上問英廉，英廉謝不知。

translations.literal: The Emperor questioned Ying Lian; Ying Lian pleaded ignorance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor questioned Ying Lian, he claimed not to know.

sentences.zh: 詔詰責，命奪職，從寬留任。

translations.literal: An edict reprimanded him; he was ordered stripped of office, but leniently allowed to remain at his post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked him and ordered his dismissal, but he was leniently permitted to keep serving.

sentences.zh: 京師商人投呈皇六子，有所陳請，事下內務府。

translations.literal: A Beijing merchant submitted a petition to the Sixth Imperial Son with certain requests; the matter was referred to the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: When a Beijing merchant petitioned the Sixth Imperial Son with a request, the case was sent down to the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 上召內務府諸大臣，問：「收呈者誰也？」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned all grand ministers of the Imperial Household Department and asked: "Who received the petition?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned the department's senior ministers and asked, "Who accepted the petition?"

sentences.zh: 英廉、金簡皆謝不知。

translations.literal: Ying Lian and Jin Jian both pleaded ignorance.
translations.idiomatic: Both Ying Lian and Jin Jian claimed ignorance.

sentences.zh: 邁拉遜乃言「六阿哥收呈」。

translations.literal: Maila Sun then said, "The Sixth Prince received the petition."
translations.idiomatic: Maila Sun then said, "The Sixth Prince took it in."

sentences.zh: 上責英廉、金簡隱諱，下部議，命寬之，仍註冊。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Ying Lian and Jin Jian for concealment; the matter was sent to the ministry for deliberation; they were ordered leniency, but the offense was still entered in the register.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor censured Ying Lian and Jin Jian for suppressing the truth; after ministry review they were treated leniently, but the offense was recorded.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was made Assistant Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 42 (1777) he became Assistant Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，暫署直隸總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he temporarily served as acting Governor-General of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 44 (1779) he acted temporarily as Governor-General of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，大學士於敏中卒，上以英廉本漢軍，協辦有年，特授漢大學士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year Grand Secretary Yu Minzhong died; because Ying Lian was originally Chinese Martial Force and had served as assistant grand secretary for years, the Emperor specially appointed him Grand Secretary of Han rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 45 (1780), after Grand Secretary Yu Minzhong died, the Emperor— noting that Ying Lian was Chinese Martial Force and had long served as assistant grand secretary— made him a Han-rank Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 漢軍授漢大學士自英廉始。

translations.literal: Appointment of a Chinese Martial Force bannerman as Han Grand Secretary began with Ying Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Lian was the first Chinese Martial Force bannerman raised to Han Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 尋授東閣大學士，仍領戶部。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary, still heading the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary while continuing to head the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，复署直隸總督，疏請清州縣虧帑。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he again served as acting Governor-General of Zhili and memorialized asking to clear county and prefectural treasury deficits.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 46 (1781) he again acted as Governor-General of Zhili and petitioned to settle shortfalls in prefectural and county treasuries.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was granted the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 47 (1782) he received the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 复署直隸總督。

translations.literal: Again he served as acting Governor-General of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He again acted as Governor-General of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 直隸災，治賑，疏請以截存漕米補各倉儲穀，又疏請蠲未完耗羨三萬馀兩，皆從其請。

translations.literal: When Zhili suffered disaster he managed relief; he memorialized to use withheld stored tribute grain to replenish granary reserves, and also memorialized to remit unpaid surplus levies of more than thirty thousand taels; all requests were granted.
translations.idiomatic: During a Zhili famine he directed relief efforts, petitioning to divert stored tribute rice to refill granaries and to waive more than thirty thousand taels in outstanding surplus fees—all approved.

sentences.zh: 尋以病乞罷，命以大學士還京師養疴。

translations.literal: Soon, on grounds of illness, he begged to retire; he was ordered to return to the capital as Grand Secretary to convalesce.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to step down for illness and was ordered home to Beijing to recuperate in his capacity as Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜白金五千治喪，祀賢良祠，諡文肅。

translations.literal: He died; five thousand taels of silver were granted for his funeral; he was enshrined in the Worthy Officials Shrine; his posthumous name was Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he received five thousand taels of silver for funeral expenses, entry into the Worthy Officials Shrine, and the posthumous name Wensu (Literary Solemn).

sentences.zh: 彭元瑞，字芸楣，江西南昌人。

translations.literal: Peng Yuanrui, style Yunmei, was a native of Nanchang, Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yuanrui, styled Yunmei, was from Nanchang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十二年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong he passed the metropolitan examination as jinshi and became a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Qianlong 22 (1757), he entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 散館授編修，直懋勤殿。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the Hanlin Academy he was appointed Compiler and served at the Maoqin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After completing Hanlin service he was made Compiler and attached to the Maoqin Hall.

sentences.zh: 大考，以內直不與。

translations.literal: At the grand examination he was excused from participation because of inner-court service.
translations.idiomatic: Exempted from the triennial evaluation because he served on the inner staff.

sentences.zh: 遷侍講。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 擢詹事府少詹事。

translations.literal: He was elevated to Junior Vice-Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Junior Vice-Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 直南書房。

translations.literal: He served at the Southern Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to the Southern Library.

sentences.zh: 遷侍郎，歷工、戶、兵、吏諸部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister, serving in succession in the Ministries of Works, Revenue, War, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Minister, serving in turn in Works, Revenue, War, and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 高宗六十壽，次聖教序為贊以進，上嘉之。

translations.literal: On the Gaozong Emperor's sixtieth birthday he composed a laudatory piece in the style of the Preface to the Sacred Teachings and presented it; the Emperor commended it.
translations.idiomatic: For the Qianlong Emperor's sixtieth birthday he wrote a hymn modeled on the Sacred Edict preface and presented it to the throne; the Emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 上製全韻詩，元瑞重次周興嗣千字文為跋。

translations.literal: The Emperor composed a poem in full rhyme; Yuanrui rearranged Zhou Xingsi's Thousand-Character Classic as a postscript.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor wrote a fully rhymed poem, Yuanrui reworked Zhou Xingsi's Thousand-Character Classic into a colophon.

sentences.zh: 上手詔獎諭，稱為「異想逸材」，賜貂裘、硯、墨。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally issued an edict of commendation, calling him "a talent of extraordinary imagination," and bestowed a sable fur coat, inkstone, and ink.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wrote him a letter of praise in his own hand, dubbing him "a mind of rare invention," and sent a sable coat, inkstone, and ink.

sentences.zh: 敕撰寧壽宮、皇極殿鐙聯，稱旨，賜以詩。

translations.literal: By imperial command he composed lantern couplets for Ningshou Palace and Huangji Hall; they met with approval, and he was granted a poem.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to write lantern-scroll couplets for Ningshou Palace and Huangji Hall, he pleased the court and received an imperial poem in return.

sentences.zh: 辟雍成，釋奠講學，又繼以耕耤。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Academy was completed, the sacrifice and lecture ceremony was held, followed in turn by the plowing ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: After the Imperial Academy opened, he took part in the sacrifice and lecture rites and then the ceremonial plowing.

sentences.zh: 上三大禮賦。

translations.literal: He presented three great ceremonial fu to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three fu celebrating the great rites to the throne.

sentences.zh: 擢尚書，歷禮、兵、吏三部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister and served successively in the Rites, War, and Personnel ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister and served in turn at Rites, War, and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，上八十壽，以歲陽在庚，進八庚全韻詩。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, when the Emperor reached his eightieth birthday, because the year's celestial stem was geng, he submitted an eight-geng complete-rhyme poem.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 55 (1790), for the Emperor's eightieth birthday, he submitted an eight-geng complete-rhyme poem, the year's stem being geng.

sentences.zh: 上以庚立字數奇，易首句用韻去一聯，末句乃諧律，親為裁定。

translations.literal: The Emperor held that counting characters by geng yielded an odd number; he changed the rhyme use in the opening line and removed one couplet, and only the final line conformed to meter—the Emperor personally settled it.
