translations.idiomatic: The Emperor found the geng-based character count awkward, revised the opening rhyme and cut a couplet so only the closing line met the meter, and settled the poem himself.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子少保、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and Associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，以從孫冒入官，御史初彭齡論劾，左授禮部侍郎，命仍直南書房。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, because a grand-nephew had fraudulently entered official service, Censor Chu Pengling memorialized in accusation; he was demoted to Vice Minister of Rites, but was ordered to continue serving in the Southern Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 56 (1791), after a grand-nephew gained office by fraud drew a memorial from Censor Chu Pengling, he was demoted to Vice Minister of Rites but kept on duty in the Southern Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 尋复授工部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，高宗奉安禮成，元瑞撰祝文，仁宗嘉其得體，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, when the rites for Gaozong's interment were completed, Yuanrui drafted the prayer text; Renzong praised its appropriateness and added him as Senior Mentor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 (1799), when Gaozong's interment rites were complete, Yuanrui's prayer text pleased Renzong, who made him Senior Mentor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 元瑞子翼蒙，官江南鹽巡道，坐事免，元瑞自劾，又坐誤舉編修繆晉，下吏議，上皆寬之。

translations.literal: Yuanrui's son Yimeng served as Jiangnan Salt Circuit intendant; he was dismissed for an offense. Yuanrui impeached himself, and was again charged with wrongly recommending Compiler Miu Jin; the matter was referred to judicial officials for deliberation, but the Emperor pardoned him in both cases.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrui's son Yimeng, intendant of the Jiangnan Salt Circuit, was dismissed for misconduct; Yuanrui impeached himself and was also charged with wrongly recommending Compiler Miu Jin—both cases went to the judicial officials, and the Emperor showed lenience in each.

sentences.zh: 修高宗實錄，命充總裁。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Record of Gaozong was being compiled, he was appointed chief editor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief editor of the Veritable Record of Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 八年，以疾乞罷，慰留，久之乃許。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he pleaded illness to resign; the Emperor urged him to stay, and only after a long while permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 8 (1803) he asked to retire on grounds of illness; the Emperor pressed him to remain, and only after long delay assented.

sentences.zh: 命仍領實錄總裁。

translations.literal: He was ordered to continue leading the Veritable Record as chief editor.
translations.idiomatic: He was still ordered to head the Veritable Record as chief editor.

sentences.zh: 旋卒，贈協辦大學士，諡文勤。

translations.literal: Soon after he died; he was posthumously granted the title Associate Grand Secretary, with the posthumous name Wenqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, and was posthumously made Associate Grand Secretary with the posthumous name Wenqin.

sentences.zh: 元瑞以文學被知遇。

translations.literal: Yuanrui won imperial favor through his literary accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrui owed his rise to imperial favor won by his literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 內廷著錄藏書及書畫、彝鼎，輯秘殿珠林、石渠寶笈、西清古鑑、寧壽鑑古、天祿琳瑯諸書，元瑞無役不與。

translations.literal: For the Inner Court cataloguing of books, calligraphy and paintings, and ritual vessels, and for the compilation of such works as Secret Hall Pearl Forest, Stone Canal Treasure Collection, Western Purification Antique Mirror, Ningshou Antique Mirror, and Tianlu Linlang, Yuanrui took part in every undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the Inner Court was cataloguing books, paintings, or bronzes, or compiling works such as Secret Hall Pearl Forest, Stone Canal Treasure Collection, Western Purification Antique Mirror, Ningshou Antique Mirror, and Tianlu Linlang, Yuanrui had a hand in every project.

sentences.zh: 和章獻頌，屢荷褒嘉。

translations.literal: He composed matching stanzas for the Zhangxian eulogy and repeatedly received praise and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: His responsive verses to the Zhangxian eulogy won repeated praise and rewards.

sentences.zh: 所著有經進藁、知聖道齋跋尾諸書。

translations.literal: His writings include Court Memorials, Postscripts from the Studio of Knowing the Sage's Way, and other works.
translations.idiomatic: Among his writings are Court Memorials and Postscripts from the Studio of Knowing the Sage's Way.

sentences.zh: 高宗實錄成，推恩賜祭，並祀賢良祠，官翼蒙員外郎。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Record of Gaozong was completed, grace was extended in bestowing sacrificial offerings, and he was also enshrined in the Worthies' Shrine; Yimeng was appointed a secretary of the sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong's Veritable Record was finished, imperial grace brought sacrificial honors and enshrinement in the Worthies' Shrine, and Yimeng was given the rank of secretary.

sentences.zh: 紀昀 紀昀，字曉嵐，直隸獻縣人。

translations.literal: Ji Yun. Ji Yun, style Xiaolan, was a native of Xian County in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yun, styled Xiaolan, was a native of Xian County in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十九年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Qianlong he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Qianlong 19 (1754) and entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 散館授編修。

translations.literal: Upon completing his Hanlin probation he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: After completing Hanlin probation he was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 再遷左春坊左庶子。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Left Sub-Reader in the Left Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Left Sub-Reader in the Left Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 京察，授貴州都勻府知府。

translations.literal: In the capital inspection he was appointed prefect of Duyun Prefecture in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital inspection he was named prefect of Duyun in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗以昀學問優，加四品銜，留庶子。

translations.literal: Gaozong, holding that Yun's learning was superior, granted him fourth-rank insignia and kept him at his post as sub-reader.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong judged Yun's learning outstanding, gave him fourth-rank insignia, and kept him as sub-reader.

sentences.zh: 尋擢翰林院侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Hanlin Academy Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 前兩淮鹽運使盧見曾得罪，昀為姻家，漏言奪職，戍烏魯木齊，釋還。

translations.literal: The former Liangjiang salt transport commissioner Lu Jianceng had fallen afoul of the throne; Yun was related by marriage and was dismissed for leaking information, exiled to Urumqi, then released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the former Liangjiang salt transport commissioner Lu Jianceng fell from favor, Yun—his kinsman by marriage—was stripped of office for leaking word, exiled to Urumqi, and later released.

sentences.zh: 上幸熱河，迎鑾密雲，試詩，以土爾扈特全部歸順為題，稱旨，复授編修。

translations.literal: When the Emperor traveled to Rehe, Yun met the imperial procession at Miyun and was examined in poetry on the topic of the complete submission of the Torghut; his work pleased the Emperor, and he was again appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor went to Rehe, Yun met the procession at Miyun and was tested in verse on the Torghuts' complete submission; his poem pleased the throne, and he was restored as compiler.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，開四庫全書館，大學士劉統勳舉昀及郎中陸錫熊為總纂。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year the Siku Quanshu project was inaugurated; Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun recommended Yun and Department Director Lu Xixiong as chief compilers.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 38 (1773), when the Siku Quanshu project opened, Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun recommended Yun and Department Director Lu Xixiong as chief compilers.

sentences.zh: 從永樂大典中搜輯散逸，盡讀諸行省所進書，論次為提要上之，擢侍讀。

translations.literal: He searched out scattered and lost texts from the Yongle Encyclopaedia, read through all books submitted from the provinces, arranged them into synopses and submitted them upward, and was promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered lost texts from the Yongle Encyclopaedia, read every book the provinces sent in, arranged synopses for submission, and was promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 上復命輯簡明書目。

translations.literal: The Emperor further ordered him to compile a concise catalogue.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also ordered him to compile a concise catalogue.

sentences.zh: 坐子汝傳積逋被訟，下吏議，上寬之。

translations.literal: Because his son Ruchuan's accumulated tax arrears were subject to lawsuit, the matter was referred to judicial officials for deliberation, but the Emperor showed leniency.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Ruchuan was sued over accumulated tax arrears, the case went to the judicial officials, but the Emperor showed leniency.

sentences.zh: 旋遷翰林院侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Hanlin Academy Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 建文淵閣藏書，命充直閣事。

translations.literal: When the Wenyuan Pavilion library was built, he was appointed to serve as a pavilion attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wenyuan Pavilion library was built, he was appointed a pavilion attendant.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he rose to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四庫全書成，表上。

translations.literal: When the Siku Quanshu was completed, the memorial of completion was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Siku Quanshu was finished, the completion memorial was submitted.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「表必出昀手！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This memorial must have come from Yun's hand!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "This memorial must be Yun's work!"

sentences.zh: 命加賚。

translations.literal: He ordered additional gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered additional rewards.

sentences.zh: 遷左都御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 再遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 復為左都御史。

translations.literal: He again became Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 畿輔災，饑民多就食京師。

translations.literal: Disaster struck the capital region, and many famine victims came to the capital seeking food.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck the capital region, hungry refugees flooded into Beijing.

sentences.zh: 故事，五城設飯廠，自十月至三月。

translations.literal: By precedent, the Five Cities established soup kitchens, operating from the tenth month through the third month.
translations.idiomatic: By longstanding practice, Beijing's Five Cities ran soup kitchens from the tenth month through the third month.

sentences.zh: 昀疏請自六月中旬始，廠日煮米三石，十月加煮米二石，仍以三月止，從之。

translations.literal: Yun submitted a memorial requesting that the kitchens begin from mid-sixth month, cooking three piculs of rice per day; from the tenth month add two piculs; still ending in the third month—the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yun memorialized that the kitchens should open from mid-sixth month, cooking three piculs of rice daily and adding two more from the tenth month, with operations still ending in the third month; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 复遷禮部尚書，仍署左都御史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of Rites, still acting as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Minister of Rites while continuing to serve as acting Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疏請鄉會試春秋罷胡安國傳，以左傳本事為文，參用公、穀，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that in the provincial and metropolitan examinations the Spring and Autumn Annals should abandon Hu Anguo's commentary, take the Zuo Tradition's original events as the basis for essays, and draw also on the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries—the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that provincial and metropolitan candidates in the Spring and Autumn Annals should set aside Hu Anguo's commentary, write essays grounded in the Zuo Tradition's narrative, and may also draw on the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，移兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 (1796) he was transferred to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 复移左都御史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二年，复遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was again transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 2 (1797) he was again made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 疏請婦女遇強暴，雖受污，仍量予旌表。

translations.literal: He memorialized that women who met with violent assault, though defiled, should still receive commemorative honors as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that women assaulted by force, though violated, should still be granted commemorative honors according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 十年，協辦大學士，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made Associate Grand Secretary and granted the title Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 10 (1805) he was made Associate Grand Secretary and Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜白金五百治喪，諡文達。

translations.literal: He died; five hundred taels of silver were granted for his funeral, and he was given the posthumous title Wenda.
translations.idiomatic: He died; the court granted five hundred taels of silver for his funeral and posthumously titled him Wenda (Literary Accomplishment).

sentences.zh: 昀學問淵通。

translations.literal: Yun's learning was profound and comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's scholarship was deep and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 撰四庫全書提要，進退百家，鉤深摘隱，各得其要指，始終條理，蔚為巨觀。

translations.literal: In composing the synopses for the Siku Quanshu, he advanced and retreated among the hundred schools, probing deep and plucking hidden points; each work obtained its essential meaning, consistently ordered throughout—a grand spectacle.
translations.idiomatic: In writing the Siku Quanshu synopses he weighed the hundred schools with discriminating judgment, probing deep and drawing out what was hidden until each work yielded its essential point; the whole, ordered from start to finish, formed a monumental achievement.

sentences.zh: 懲明季講學之習，宋五子書功令所重，不敢顯立異同；

translations.literal: Chastising the late-Ming habit of public lecturing, and with the books of the Five Song Masters being what the examination system prized, he dared not openly declare agreement or disagreement;
translations.idiomatic: Wary of the late-Ming passion for public lecturing and of the examination system's esteem for the Five Song Masters, he dared not openly take sides;

sentences.zh: 而於南宋以後諸儒，深文詆諆，不無門戶出入之見云。

translations.literal: Yet toward Confucians after the Southern Song, he used harsh language of denunciation, not without partisan bias in choosing whom to admit or exclude.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in treating Southern Song and later scholars, he often wrote in harshly denunciatory tones—not without partisan favor in deciding who belonged and who did not.

sentences.zh: 陸錫熊，字健男，江蘇上海人。

translations.literal: Lu Xixiong, style Jiannan, was a native of Shanghai, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xixiong, styled Jiannan, came from Shanghai in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He earned jinshi in Qianlong 26 (1761).

sentences.zh: 召試，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: Called to examination, he was appointed a Grand Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to an imperial examination, he was appointed a drafter in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 累遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he rose to department director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to department director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 與昀同司總纂，旋並授翰林院侍讀。

translations.literal: He served with Yun as chief compiler; soon both were appointed Hanlin Academy readers.
translations.idiomatic: He served with Yun as chief compiler, and both were soon appointed Hanlin readers.

sentences.zh: 五遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: After five promotions he became Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he became Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 旋以書有譌謬，令重為校正，寫官所費，責錫熊與昀分任。

translations.literal: Soon, because the books contained errors, he was ordered to recorrect them; the copyists' expenses were charged to Xixiong and Yun to share.
translations.idiomatic: When errors were found in the books, he was ordered to recorrect them, and the copyists' costs were split between Xixiong and Yun.

sentences.zh: 又令詣奉天校正文溯閣藏書，卒於奉天。

translations.literal: He was further ordered to go to Mukden to collate the books stored in the Wenshu Pavilion, and died in Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent to Mukden to collate the Wenshu Pavilion collection and died there.

sentences.zh: 陸費墀，字丹叔，浙江桐鄉人。

translations.literal: Lu Feichi, style Danshu, was a native of Tongxiang, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Feichi, styled Danshu, came from Tongxiang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 陸費為複姓。

translations.literal: Lu Fei is a compound surname.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fei is a compound surname.

sentences.zh: 墀，乾隆三十一年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Feichi passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-first year of Qianlong, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Feichi earned jinshi in Qianlong 31 (1766), entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 充四庫全書館總校，用昀、錫熊例，擢侍讀。

translations.literal: He served as chief proofreader of the Siku Quanshu project; following the precedent of Yun and Xixiong, he was promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: As chief proofreader of the Siku Quanshu project, he was promoted to reader on the same terms as Yun and Xixiong.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he rose to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 書有譌謬，上謂昀、錫熊、墀專司其事，而墀咎尤重。

translations.literal: When the books contained errors, the Emperor said Yun, Xixiong, and Feichi were specially charged with the matter, but Feichi bore the heavier blame.
translations.idiomatic: When errors were found in the books, the Emperor held that Yun, Xixiong, and Feichi were specially responsible, but Feichi bore the heaviest blame.

sentences.zh: 文瀾、文匯、文宗三閣書面葉木匣，責墀出資裝治。

translations.literal: The wooden cases for the page leaves of the books in the Wenlan, Wenhui, and Wenzong pavilions—Feichi was charged to fund their binding and repair.
translations.idiomatic: Feichi was ordered to pay for the wooden cases and binding of the books at the Wenlan, Wenhui, and Wenzong pavilions.

sentences.zh: 仍下吏議，奪職。

translations.literal: The matter was still referred to the judicial officials for deliberation, and he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: The case was still sent to the judicial officials for review, and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 旋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 上命籍墀家，留千金贍其孥，馀充三閣裝治之用。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Feichi's household goods confiscated; one thousand taels were kept to support his wife and children, and the remainder applied to binding the three pavilions' books.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Feichi's estate confiscated, kept one thousand taels to support his wife and children, and applied the rest to binding the books at the three pavilions.

sentences.zh: 論曰：乾隆中年後，多以武功致台鼎。

translations.literal: The commentary says: After the middle years of Qianlong, many reached the highest ministerial offices through military merit.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: After mid-Qianlong, many men reached the highest offices through military achievement.

sentences.zh: 若三寶、永貴、國治、英廉，皆先陟外台，敭歷著聲績。

translations.literal: Such men as San Bao, Yong Gui, Guozhi, and Ying Lian all first rose through provincial posts, repeatedly passing through offices and achieving renown.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as San Bao, Yong Gui, Guozhi, and Ying Lian all first rose through provincial service, repeatedly passing through posts and achieving renown.

sentences.zh: 國治直樞廷十馀年，先後與於敏中、和珅未嘗有所阿。

translations.literal: Guozhi served directly at the inner court for more than ten years; serving in succession with Yu Minzhong and Heshen, he never showed partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhi served at the inner court for more than ten years; whether alongside Yu Minzhong or Heshen, he never showed favoritism.

sentences.zh: 新、元瑞、昀起侍從，文學負時望。

translations.literal: Xin, Yuanrui, and Yun rose from attendant service; their literary attainments commanded contemporary esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, Yuanrui, and Yun rose from service at court; their literary gifts commanded the age's respect.

sentences.zh: 新謹厚承世遠之教。

translations.literal: Xin was cautious and sincere, inheriting Shi Yuan's teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was careful and steadfast, carrying on the teachings of Shi Yuan.

sentences.zh: 昀校定四庫書，成一代文治，允哉，稱其位矣！

translations.literal: Yun collated the Siku books and achieved an age of literary governance—indeed, his title matched his station!
translations.idiomatic: Yun collated the Siku collection and brought about an age of literary governance—truly, he was worthy of his place!
